newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - SPAIN'S JULY CPI UP 1.6 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - SPAIN'S JULY CPI UP 1.6 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions after Spain reported July consumer inflation up 0.2 percent and up 1.6 percent year-on-year, as expected. Core July inflation rose 0.2 percent and 2.0 percent year-on-year.
HEATHER RICHARDSON, ECONOMIST AT UBS LTD IN LONDON
"The numbers were in line with our forecasts and with what the market expected as well.
"The Bank of Spain has scope to cut rates but not at this meeting. I think they will wait for August CPI.

"The underlying was slightly higher than expected. We had 0.2 percent, which translated into 1.9 percent so, it must have been 0.23 or so. We are at three-month highs but considering we were at 3.5 percent last year, it's still very low. We expect it to stay around two percent and maybe tick up to 2.2 percent or 2.3 percent."
COLIN WARREN, ECONOMIST AT TOKAI BANK, LONDON

"Services inflation is pretty horrendous really...with a good tourist season and strong sterling, people are on a spending spree and they're taking advantage to put their prices up. Services inflation (excluding rents 0.7 percent versus June, 3.7 percent year-on-year) is at its highest level since the first quarter of 1996...headline (inflation) rates have come down, but they've made no progress on the services and tourism front...This makes the Bank of Spain's task more difficult. If we weren't in a situation where they have to converge (for monetary union), people would be talking about them taking the heat out of the recovery."
